title: Occupation of territory, Handing over of Towns to the descendents of Bhai Bhagtoo and Bhai Phool and About…

blocks.text: Dohra:

After ransacking and plundering the city of Sirhind, Morale of the Khalsa Panth forces increased manifold. Listen to the developments which took place thereafter, As both factions of the Khalsa panth went on their own ways. (1)
lines: After ransacking and plundering the city of Sirhind,
Morale of the Khalsa Panth forces increased manifold.
Listen to the developments which took place thereafter,
As both factions of the Khalsa panth went on their own ways.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Buddha Dal1 Singhs opined that the Khalsa must march towards Delhi, But Taruna Dal2 Singhs favoured returning towards Lahore. Someone opined that the Khalsa should occupy the hills, Another stated that the Khalsa should ransack the South. (2)
lines: Buddha Dal1 Singhs opined that the Khalsa must march towards Delhi,
But Taruna Dal2 Singhs favoured returning towards Lahore.
Someone opined that the Khalsa should occupy the hills,
Another stated that the Khalsa should ransack the South.

blocks.text: Different factions expressing different strategic maneuvers, Each faction searched for a favourable territory for occupation. Buddha Dal marching forward moved ahead (towards Delhi), Taruna Dal retreated the path they had come forward. (3)
lines: Different factions expressing different strategic maneuvers,
Each faction searched for a favourable territory for occupation.
Buddha Dal marching forward moved ahead (towards Delhi),
Taruna Dal retreated the path they had come forward.

blocks.text: As Taruna Dal laid a siege to the city of Lahore, Buddha Dal launched an attack towards Delhi. The big cities as were located on the way to Delhi, These cities were ransacked by the Khalsa Panth forces. (4)
lines: As Taruna Dal laid a siege to the city of Lahore,
Buddha Dal launched an attack towards Delhi.
The big cities as were located on the way to Delhi,
These cities were ransacked by the Khalsa Panth forces.

blocks.text: Thus did Buddha Dal force reach the city of Azimabad, Which, since the beginning, was known as Taravari3 . Putting up a camp here after ransacking the city, They marched forward at the break of the next dawn. (5)
lines: Thus did Buddha Dal force reach the city of Azimabad,
Which, since the beginning, was known as Taravari3 .
Putting up a camp here after ransacking the city,
They marched forward at the break of the next dawn.

blocks.text: Dohra:

S. Shyam Singh, the Buddha Dal chief, had delegated his powers, S. Karora Singh4 had he made an incharge of his force. Being on a hunting expedition in the surrounding area, Inadvertently had he reached near an old inn. (6)
lines: S.
Shyam Singh, the Buddha Dal chief, had delegated his powers,
S.
Karora Singh4 had he made an incharge of his force.
Being on a hunting expedition in the surrounding area,
Inadvertently had he reached near an old inn.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

An inn there was which was huge and strongly built, With Banda Bahadur's great efforts was it built. As it sheltered a large number of Mughal soldiers, One of these soldiers fired a bullet from inside the inn. (7)
lines: An inn there was which was huge and strongly built,
With Banda Bahadur's great efforts was it built.
As it sheltered a large number of Mughal soldiers,
One of these soldiers fired a bullet from inside the inn.

blocks.text: This bullet that was fired hit S. Krora Singh's body, Who, having died instantly, was cremated on the mound there. Next day, the Khalsa Panth force, marched ahead, Ransacking any other city which fell on their route. (8)
lines: This bullet that was fired hit S.
Krora Singh's body,
Who, having died instantly, was cremated on the mound there.
Next day, the Khalsa Panth force, marched ahead,
Ransacking any other city which fell on their route.

blocks.text: After ransacking and occupying the cities of Hansi and Hissar5 , The Khalsa Panth forces returned towards Jind and Karnal. Thus upto the Yamuna river and upto the foot hills in the north, Khalsa Panth raised walled shelters and fortifications. (9)
lines: After ransacking and occupying the cities of Hansi and Hissar5 ,
The Khalsa Panth forces returned towards Jind and Karnal.
Thus upto the Yamuna river and upto the foot hills in the north,
Khalsa Panth raised walled shelters and fortifications.

blocks.text: Full five Misls were the Khalsa forces of Majhail Singhs, Sixth was the Misl of Malwa Singhs who had joined them. These Malwa Singhs were accorded the status of Sikh subjects, After receiving a ransom from them for ruling this area. (10)
lines: Full five Misls were the Khalsa forces of Majhail Singhs,
Sixth was the Misl of Malwa Singhs who had joined them.
These Malwa Singhs were accorded the status of Sikh subjects,
After receiving a ransom from them for ruling this area.

blocks.text: Dohra:

(These Malwa Singhs were made custodians of the territory), Which included territories of Patiala and Nabha States. As well as the territories of Jind and Kaithal states. Including villages of Ballowal6 , Bhadaur7 , Senna8 and Mehraj9 . (11)
lines: (These Malwa Singhs were made custodians of the territory),
Which included territories of Patiala and Nabha States.
As well as the territories of Jind and Kaithal states.
Including villages of Ballowal6 ,
Bhadaur7 ,
Senna8 and Mehraj9 .

blocks.text: Moreover, the Brars were divided into two factions, Belonging to the regions of Sabo10 and Banwal" . Their factions, being at loggerheads with each other, They were allotted territories after negotiated deals. (12)
lines: Moreover, the Brars were divided into two factions,
Belonging to the regions of Sabo10 and Banwal" .
Their factions, being at loggerheads with each other,
They were allotted territories after negotiated deals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Those Singhs belonging to dynasties of Baba Phool12 and Bhai Bhagtoo13 , They came forward as the Khalsa Panth forces reached there. A large tract of land was reserved for cattle grazing, So that Khalsa's horses and cattle may freely roam about. (13)
lines: Those Singhs belonging to dynasties of Baba Phool12 and Bhai Bhagtoo13 ,
They came forward as the Khalsa Panth forces reached there.
A large tract of land was reserved for cattle grazing,
So that Khalsa's horses and cattle may freely roam about.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the Buddha Dal Singhs put up a camp at Sirhind, Demolishing the Mughal forts following Guru's instructions. They dug up the foundations and demolished the Mughal forts, Partially following Guru's instructions partially for their own gains. (14)
lines: Thereafter, the Buddha Dal Singhs put up a camp at Sirhind,
Demolishing the Mughal forts following Guru's instructions.
They dug up the foundations and demolished the Mughal forts,
Partially following Guru's instructions partially for their own gains.

blocks.text: And those Brars from the Talwandi Sabo area, They were made to pay ransom to the Khalsa Panth. And those Brars belonging to Banwal area, They, too, were made to abide by the Khalsa dictates. (15)
lines: And those Brars from the Talwandi Sabo area,
They were made to pay ransom to the Khalsa Panth.
And those Brars belonging to Banwal area,
They, too, were made to abide by the Khalsa dictates.

blocks.text: Horses, revenues would these Brars send to Khalsa Panth, Even their own houses would they offer at the time of war. Thus did all the Singhs unite in perfect harmony, Many developing family bonds and many getting initiated. (16)
lines: Horses, revenues would these Brars send to Khalsa Panth,
Even their own houses would they offer at the time of war.
Thus did all the Singhs unite in perfect harmony,
Many developing family bonds and many getting initiated.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Many of these Brars partook Khandey-ki-Pahul, As they were influenced by the Khalsa Panth's conduct. They, too, became recipients' of Guru's blessings after initiation, Though they had not worked hard to be worthy of it. (17)
lines: Many of these Brars partook Khandey-ki-Pahul,
As they were influenced by the Khalsa Panth's conduct.
They, too, became recipients' of Guru's blessings after initiation,
Though they had not worked hard to be worthy of it.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Those verses from Sri Guru Granth described them best, Which formed a part of the verses from Sukhmani14 . Company of the saints compensates for all sorts of hard work, A glimpse of their divine face blesses those around them. (18)
lines: Those verses from Sri Guru Granth described them best,
Which formed a part of the verses from Sukhmani14 .
Company of the saints compensates for all sorts of hard work,
A glimpse of their divine face blesses those around them.

blocks.text: Many a Muslim, too, opted to stay in the Khalsa territory, Readily they became subjects and paid revenues willingly. Whatever territory came into possession of individual Singhs, Those territories did they occupy making concerted efforts. (19)
lines: Many a Muslim, too, opted to stay in the Khalsa territory,
Readily they became subjects and paid revenues willingly.
Whatever territory came into possession of individual Singhs,
Those territories did they occupy making concerted efforts.

blocks.text: Territorial custody which was under Nawab Jain Khan's15 control, Whole of it was ransacked and revenue collected from it. The Pathans inhabitants of Malerkotla were not touched, Vindicating Guru's words without any breach of trust. (20)
lines: Territorial custody which was under Nawab Jain Khan's15 control,
Whole of it was ransacked and revenue collected from it.
The Pathans inhabitants of Malerkotla were not touched,
Vindicating Guru's words without any breach of trust.

blocks.text: Land revenue would the Singhs collect after surrounding a village, Which the descendents of Sher Mohammad16 would readily offer. A territory consisting of one hundred villages was spared for Pathans, Every year each village had to offer one horse to the Singhs. (21)
lines: Land revenue would the Singhs collect after surrounding a village,
Which the descendents of Sher Mohammad16 would readily offer.
A territory consisting of one hundred villages was spared for Pathans,
Every year each village had to offer one horse to the Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Ten Khalsa Panth Misls took a united decision, That this territory be kept under a joint control. It being a resting place for the coming and going Khalsa forces, It should be named a "Beer" common to all. (22)
lines: Ten Khalsa Panth Misls took a united decision,
That this territory be kept under a joint control.
It being a resting place for the coming and going Khalsa forces,
It should be named a "Beer" common to all.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

There was one feudal lord (Rai) from Jagraon17 , Who joined the Khalsa Panth along with his force. He had been an ally of the Khalsa from the beginning, His ambassadors had always followed the Khalsa edicts. (23)
lines: There was one feudal lord (Rai) from Jagraon17 ,
Who joined the Khalsa Panth along with his force.
He had been an ally of the Khalsa from the beginning,
His ambassadors had always followed the Khalsa edicts.

blocks.text: The revenues that he had been paying to the Mughals so far, He agreed to pay that revenue to the Khalsa Panth. The Khalsa Panth also had a similar conciliatory policy, So that it could keep common control over the territory. (24)
lines: The revenues that he had been paying to the Mughals so far,
He agreed to pay that revenue to the Khalsa Panth.
The Khalsa Panth also had a similar conciliatory policy,
So that it could keep common control over the territory.

blocks.text: Three territories were decided to be kept as common lands, So that the horses of both could freely graze there. The whole Khalsa Panth would not ransack these territories, As these would be a launching pad for Khalsa forces. (25)
lines: Three territories were decided to be kept as common lands,
So that the horses of both could freely graze there.
The whole Khalsa Panth would not ransack these territories,
As these would be a launching pad for Khalsa forces.

blocks.text: Rest of the territory was occupied according to one's convenience, Whosoever occupied it was powerful, the rest weaker. Whosoever looked after their subjects lovingly, He, too, was loved and patronized by his subjects. (26)
lines: Rest of the territory was occupied according to one's convenience,
Whosoever occupied it was powerful, the rest weaker.
Whosoever looked after their subjects lovingly,
He, too, was loved and patronized by his subjects.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Bhai Bhagtoo's descendents and those from Mehraj, Together with Rajput Muslim converts and Pathans, They agreed to keep some territory as common lands, Where Khalsa forces could rest on their way to Delhi. (27)
lines: Bhai Bhagtoo's descendents and those from Mehraj,
Together with Rajput Muslim converts and Pathans,
They agreed to keep some territory as common lands,
Where Khalsa forces could rest on their way to Delhi.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

If any misl ventured to occupy that common land, Two more Misls would gang up in their support. The Muslim chiefs also got wind of Khalsa Misl's weakness, Thus would the Khalsa Misls be divided through payment of ransoms. (28)
lines: If any misl ventured to occupy that common land,
Two more Misls would gang up in their support.
The Muslim chiefs also got wind of Khalsa Misl's weakness,
Thus would the Khalsa Misls be divided through payment of ransoms.

blocks.text: So listen to this account my dear Captain David Murray, So have I narrated as I have heard it said. My father, who had been a close associate of Khalsa Panth, So had he narrated the whole account to me. (29)
lines: So listen to this account my dear Captain David Murray,
So have I narrated as I have heard it said.
My father, who had been a close associate of Khalsa Panth,
So had he narrated the whole account to me.
